What Is a Trademark? And Its Importance

Any distinctive sign that differentiates a business’s goods or services from others is called a trademark in the UAE. It could be a name, logo, word, symbol, or combination. Trademarks are legally protected once registered. Gives the owner rights to prevent unauthorized use within the country.

Take it as the oxygen for your brand. It’s your brand’s identity that makes your product different from others. Every product, whether it’s a bat or a ball, must have a unique identity. Your product can’t survive longer if it lacks a trademark behind it. It protects your brand identity legally. The benefit? No one else can copy or misuse it.

The moment you register your trademark, it gives your business exclusive rights. You can utilize it to build your customer trust. Having a registered brand on hand prevents you from legal disputes. You never came across brand confusion. Your business value ultimately strengthens when you register a trademark.

What Qualifies for Trademark?

Article 2 of Federal Decree-Law states:

Any distinctive sign capable of distinguishing goods is termed a trademark. Most people think of logos and names. However, the law goes further than this.

Traditional trademarks include:

Brand names, logos and symbols, slogans and taglines, and colors or combinations of colors.

Non-traditional trademarks:

3D shapes, e.g., product packaging, holograms, sounds like audio branding, and even smells if they can be defined. This expansion aligns the UAE with global IP standards. Opens creative opportunities for modern brands.

What Can’t Be Registered as a Trademark?

Article 3 sets clean boundaries. Your application will be rejected if it includes:

Prohibited Category Explanation
Generic or Descriptive Terms Terms that describe the product/service (e.g., “Coffee Shop” for a café)
Violation of Public Morals or Order Any offensive mark or against public values
National Flags & Official Symbols Includes the UAE flag or symbols of international bodies
Religious Symbols Any mark containing religious signs or sacred references
Geographically Misleading Names Marks that falsely suggest a product originates from a specific place
Identical or Similar Existing Marks Trademarks that are already registered or too similar.

Many applications fail due to this. This doesn’t happen because your brand is weak. But it occurs as it conflicts legally.

Why Register Your UAE Trademark? Benefits Explained

Trademark registration is not only paperwork. It’s more than that. Consider it a leverage. Out of so many benefits of trademark registration in the UAE, it gives you exclusive legal rights within the seven emirates. If you take registration for granted, enforcement becomes difficult and uncertain.

Brand registration protects you from counterfeiting and imitation. These are the real risks in sectors of high-growth like:

  • Retail
  • E-commerce
  • Tech.

Your trademark becomes a commercial asset. You can license it, franchise it, or even sell it. A great way to turn your brand into revenue. Further, a trademark enables customs enforcement. You can record your trademark with Dubai, Sharjah, and RAK customs authorities. This way, you can block counterfeit imports. A brand trademark opens the door to international protection via the Madrid Protocol.

Simply put, trademark registration transforms your brand. A transformation from an idea into protected IP in the UAE.

How to Conduct a Trademark Search Before Filing?

Be sure to check it before regretting it afterwards. Making this mistake will cost you in terms of rejection and losing filing fees. Sometimes, you face a legal dispute with the original owner. So, take a trademark search in the UAE on a priority level.

Why is it Non-Negotiable?

Filing without a search is like signing a contract without reading it. You risk immediate rejection and loss of filing fees. Sometimes, legal disputes with existing owners arise. There’s a misconception regarding trademark rules that registering a trade name on your business license gives you trademark rights. In actuality, it does not. Both trade names and trademarks are separate systems. Only a registered trademark grants legal ownership. Brand protection is guaranteed.

Trademark Registry Search Steps:

Thinking about how to check a trademark in the UAE?

Gain clarity here, step by step:

  1. MoE eServices Portal

This is the official UAE government platform. It provides a legally valid trademark search. The MoE eServices Portal is a paid service that costs you around 350 dirhams and should always be your primary check before filing.

  1. WIPO Global Brand Database

WIPO is a free international database. It helps you identify existing global trademarks that could conflict with your application in the UAE.

  1. TMview

A free tool covering multiple regions. GCC and EU trademarks come under it. Quite useful for spotting regional conflicts beyond the UAE.

Start risk-free by combining all three before filing.

Trademark Registration Process, UAE:

The UAE trademark registration process is simple if you know how to do it. The steps are discussed below for your better understanding.

how to register a trademark in the UAE

Step 1 —> Conduct a Trademark Search

Trademark search is the very first step that you can’t miss at any cost. How to do it? We have already talked about it earlier in the blog.

Step 2 —> Select the Right Trademark Class

The UAE uses the Nice Classification system, 13th Edition for 2026. Each class means a separate application plus a fee.

Examples:

  • Class 35 → Retail, advertising, marketing
  • Class 42 → Technology and software services
  • Class 25 → Clothing and apparel

The wrong class selection can either leave your brand unprotected or force you to reapply. The reapplication step involves extra cost.

Step 3 —> Prepare Your Documents

The document preparation step is another important step that needs consideration. You’ll need:

  • Notarized Power of Attorney
  • Passport / Emirates ID of the owner
  • Trade license copy
  • Trademark logo (JPG/PDF)
  • List of goods/services with class numbers

Foreign applicants must file through a trademark agent.

Step 4 —> File the Application via MoE Portal

Submit applications online via the Ministry of Economy portal. The authority reviews formal compliance and conflicts with existing marks. They check the distinctiveness after which they give it a green signal. The process takes thirty to ninety days.

Step 5 —> Publication & Opposition Period

Your trademark is published in the Official Gazette upon approval. The opposition window opens for thirty days. In that period, if opposition is filed, you must respond legally. If not, the application proceeds to registration.

Step 6 —> Pay Registration Fees & Receive Certificate

After the opposition period passes, you are required to pay the final fees. Then, the certificate will be issued within thirty days. The validity remains up to ten years from the filing date.

Trademark Registration Cost in UAE: Updated Fees

The UAE trademark fees are a must to know beforehand. Knowing it lately will delay your process or cause you rejection.

Standard Official Fee Breakdown (Per Class)

Stage Fee in Dirhams
Filing Fee 750
Publication Fee 750
Registration Fee 5,665
Total 7,165 Dirhams

SME & People of Determination Discounts:

The UAE government has introduced huge fee concessions, making brand protection more accessible. Registered businesses under the National Program can receive a 50 percent discount on trademark fees. Whereas, People of Determination are granted a 100 percent exemption.

The incentives are designed for employers. It’s an encouragement for their entrepreneurship journey. It removes financial barriers. These barriers usually prevent individuals/small businesses from securing their trademark rights.

Expedited Examination Option

The expedited examination option was introduced on November 14, 2025. It allows priority review of trademark applications within 1 working day. It costs around 2,250 dirhams. A great step for urgent product launches or time-sensitive brand registrations.

Additional Costs to Budget For

Some of the extra costs that can interfere with the process are Arabic translations, opposition/legal responses, appeal fees, and consultant fees.

Trademark Validity & Renewal:

Worry about your brand’s trademark validity? You have plenty of time to enjoy ownership. You don’t require trademark renewal in the UAE for ten years. Your trademark remains valid for 10 years from filing. Renew it indefinitely after it expires.

In case of taking a step late, you may face late renewal penalties. You are charged around 100 dirhams per month for the publication delay. In case of a registration delay, you have to bear 1,000 dirhams per month. If unused for 5 consecutive years, your trademark can be cancelled.

Register a UAE Trademark Internationally: The Madrid Protocol Route

The UAE’s accession in 2021 gives businesses the authority to secure international trademark protection through a single application. In which you can file one trademark and extend protection within multiple member countries. Renewals are managed centrally. This makes global brand expansion steadier.

A trademark only protects your brand within the UAE. It does not cover other GCC countries. The Madrid Protocol UAE trademark is what helps bridge that international protection gap. So ask yourself what your business goals are, and according to them, make a move!

Everything To Know About UAE Trademark Law:

Under the UAE trademark law:

Protection is governed by Federal Decree-Law No. 36 of 2021. This sets the legal framework for registration and trademark owners’ rights. The law is further implemented through Cabinet Resolution No. 57 of 2022. It outlines the procedures and implementation rules. Trademark applications are handled by the UAE Ministry of Economy. The MOE is the official authority responsible for managing and enforcing trademark rights in the country. The UAE operates on a registration-based system. Whereas unregistered trademarks have limited protection.

Fines and legal action are included as penalties for infringement under the 2021 law.

FAQs

Q1: How much does it cost to register a trademark in the UAE?

Registering a trademark costs 7,165 dirhams, which is equal to $ 1,950 per class. The professional fees are excluded.

Q2: How long does trademark registration take in the UAE?

Trademark registration takes around four to six months. The objections and processing decide the actual time.

Q3: Can a foreigner register a trademark in the UAE?

Foreigners can register a trademark. However, they must apply through a UAE-registered trademark agent.

Q4: What can’t be registered as a trademark in the UAE?

Listing down some of the things that you should keep in mind. These have never been registered as a trademark in the UAE.

  • Generic names
  • Religious symbols
  • State emblems
  • Misleading marks
  • Identical existing trademarks.

Q5: Do I need to do a trademark search before applying in the UAE?

It’s very risky if you miss a trademark search before applying. Skipping it risks you in the form of rejection, lost fees, and legal issues.

Q6: How do I renew my UAE trademark?

You can renew your trademark every 10 years via the Ministry of Economy. Late fees apply if delayed.

Q7: Does a UAE trademark protect my brand in other countries?

The trademark doesn’t protect your brand in other countries. You need international protection via the Madrid Protocol.

Q8: What is the Nice Classification system, and which edition applies?

Nice classification is a global system categorizing goods/services. The United Arab Emirates uses the 13th Edition 2026.
